sentences.text: Counter affidavit filed by the complainant/informant is taken on record.

2. Heard Shri Manoj Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the accused/applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as Ms. Garima Singh, learned counsel appearing for the complainant/informant and perused the record.

3. This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Rajjab Ali for grant of bail, in Case Crime No. 100 of 2023, under Sections 376,498A,323,504,506 IPC & Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Fakharpur, District Bahraich, during trial.

4. Learned counsel for the accused-applicant while pressing the bail application submits that the accused-applicant has falsely been implicated in the instant case and he has not committed any offence as claimed by the prosecution.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the FIR of this case was lodged by the prosecutrix/victim herself wherein the allegations with regard to the demand of dowry and committing cruelty in lieu thereof have been levelled and there is no whisper about the rape.
However, in her statement recorded U/s 161 & 164 CrPC, for the very first time, the factum of rape has been alleged against the applicant who is the father-in-law of the informant/complainant.

6. It is vehemently submitted that a simple matrimonial dispute has been given the colour of rape and had there been any offence committed by the applicant pertaining to sexual assault, the same would have found place in the FIR itself.

7. It is also submitted that the informant/victim herself refused to undergo any internal medical examination and thus, in support of the allegations of rape, there is only untrustworthy and uncorroborated statement of the informant/victim.

8. While drawing attention of the Court towards the Annexure No. 5 which appears to be a copy of 'Bedakhlinama' allegedly executed by the instant applicant, it is submitted that by execution of the document, the applicant had ousted the husband of the informant and the informant/victim from his house and it is on this basis, the instant FIR has been lodged against him.
9.
It is further submitted that the applicant is in jail in this case since 7.5.2023 and he is not having any criminal antecedents.
Charge sheet in the matter has already been filed and there is no apprehension that the accused-applicant after release on bail, may flee from the process of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.
10. Learned A.G.A., on the other hand submits that having manner on which the offence has been committed the applicant is not entitled for any relief.

11. Ms. Garima Singh, learned counsel appearing for the informant/victim submits that the informant/victim belongs to the rural background and therefore, if the factum of rape is not found in the FIR, the same may not be taken adverse to her as she has stated about commission of rape by the instant applicant in her statement recorded U/s 161 & 164 CrPC.
12.
Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is transpired that the informant/victim is the daughter-in-law of the applicant.
Admittedly, she is having strained relations with her husband.

The allegations have been levelled in the FIR, with regard to demand of dowry and committing cruelty in lieu thereof against all the accused persons named in the FIR and the allegation against the applicant is only of having a bad eye on the informant/victim.

However,
there is no whisper about the commission of any molestation or rape by the applicant.
In her statement recorded U/s 161 & 164 CrPC, for the very first time, the factum of rape has been asserted/levelled against the applicant.
It is vehemently submitted on behalf of the applicant that matrimonial dispute existing between husband and wife has been given the colour of rape.
Reliance has also been placed on the 'Bedakhlinama' whereby the applicant has ousted the informant/victim and her husband (the son of the applicant) from his house.
The applicant is in jail in this case since 7.5.2023 without any criminal history.
Charge sheet in the matter has already been filed.

13. Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits and demerits of the case, I am of the considered view that applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

14. Let the applicant- Rajjab Ali involved in the aforesaid case be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
15.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
16. Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
17. Observations made herein-above are only for the purpose of disposal of bail application and the same shall not have any bearing on the trial of the case.
